sections.html:
Charleston is West Virginia's capital and biggest city, laid out along the Kanawha River at the mouth of the Elk. It is the seat of Kanawha County. The 2025 estimate puts the population at 46,117, down from 48,864 in 2020 and 85,796 at the 1960 peak. Urban renewal in the 1960s cleared many buildings, the Triangle District especially, and some vacant lots from that era remain.

Fifteen named neighborhoods fill the city, among them the East End and Edgewood historic districts, the West Side, South Hills, Kanawha City, Elk City, Fort Hill, Forest Hills and North Charleston, plus Charleston Heights, Louden Heights, Riverview, Shadowlawn, South Park and South Ruffner. House age and flood exposure shift from one to the next, so give the neighborhood when you ask a city office about an address.

Government and health care anchor jobs here. Charleston Area Medical Center, formed in 1972 from the major hospitals, serves southern West Virginia, and the chemical industry is far smaller than it once was.

Of everything about the local setting, flooding does the most to shape a sale. The city's floodplain office counts 13 floods larger than the 1 percent annual chance flood, the last in 1934, and smaller events have done damage too. The Floodplain Manager reviews building permits and can tell you whether an address sits in a Special Flood Hazard Area. In those areas flood insurance is typically required.

An Elevation Certificate from a surveyor or engineer can help set premiums and can back a map amendment request. Charleston is the only municipality in West Virginia in the Community Rating System, at Class 9, which earns a 5 percent premium discount. Water in the Kanawha River above 123,000 cubic feet per second floods low-lying areas, and flow above 155,000 floods the mapped flood zones.

Start with the city floodplain management page and the state's flood hazard tool. Run any address before you price the house, since buyers and their lenders will.

sections.h2: Permits and repairs before you sell
sections.html:
Construction in Charleston needs a permit before work starts. The Building Department lets homeowners do their own work if the permit is pulled and an inspection shows the work meets code. Roofs, replacement windows, siding, fences, retaining walls, driveways, plumbing, electrical and HVAC all fall under the rule.

  • Permit fees are waived when the total job cost is $2,500 or less.
  • A contractor who starts without a permit pays at least $100 or twice the normal fee, whichever is greater, and faces a license suspension of at least three months.
  • A demolition permit calls for an asbestos report and details on capping the storm and sewer laterals.
  • Applications go to the Permit Coordinator, Building Department, 915 Quarrier Street, Suite 5. The permit office number is 304-348-6833.

These rules cover repairs you make to get ready for a sale, and a buyer's inspector may ask about any work done without a permit. A cash sale skips most of that back and forth, because the buyer takes the house as it stands.

sections.h2: Who bills and who values your home
sections.html:
The county bills property tax here, not the city. The Kanawha County Sheriff's Tax Division collects, and the Kanawha County Assessor sets values.

OfficeAddress and hoursPhone
Kanawha County Sheriff's Tax Office409 Virginia Street East, Room 120, Charleston, WV 25301; Monday to Friday, 8:00 to 5:00304-357-0210
Kanawha County AssessorKanawha County Courthouse, 409 Virginia Street East304-357-0250

The tax office also runs detachments in Cross Lanes, Sissonville, Elkview, Jefferson and Quincy. It mails roughly 100,000 real estate tickets and 95,000 personal property tickets every July.

sections.h2: Due dates, discounts and tax classes
sections.html:
Kanawha County uses the state calendar. Tickets go out on or after July 15, and each half is due on September 1 or March 1. Pay before either date for a 2.5 percent discount. Halves turn delinquent on October 1 and April 1, and late tax draws 9 percent interest a year.

Class matters for the rate. Owner-occupied residential property is Class II, taxed at two times the Class I rate. Other property inside a municipality, a rental for example, is Class IV at four times the Class I rate. Ask the assessor which class your house carries before you work out what a buyer will owe.

sections.h2: Transfer tax and other closing costs
sections.html:
The main government charge at closing is the transfer tax recorded with the deed. West Virginia Code 11-22-2 sets it at $1.10 per $500 of value, kept by the county since July 1, 2025. An additional county tax of 55 cents per $500 applies unless the commission has raised it, and a $20 fee covers transfers for consideration.

The grantor pays unless the grantee accepts the deed with the tax unpaid. Overdue property tax, an earlier mortgage and any liens come out of the proceeds, so ask the sheriff's office for the tax status before you accept any number.

Older houses, homes near the Kanawha and Elk rivers, and inherited properties are the situations sellers in Charleston plan for most. The East End and Edgewood carry historic district designations, and river-side homes raise the flood questions above.

You can list, sell by owner or sell for cash, and each route treats those issues differently. A listing brings showings and buyer financing. A cash sale usually means a title search, payoff of any liens and a deed recorded with the county. Before you pick, bring these to the first conversation:

  • your most recent tax ticket and the sheriff's balance
  • the deed, and the probate paperwork if the house was inherited
  • any permit records for work done on the house
  • a floodplain determination if the house sits near water

At closing the title company pays off liens and open tax from your proceeds, the deed goes to the county for recording, and you receive what remains. If a payoff turns out larger than you expected, you will want to learn that before you sign a contract, not at the table.

Compare what each route leaves you after taxes, liens and transfer costs, and not the headline price alone.

Interstates 64, 77 and 79 cross Charleston, and the West Virginia Turnpike ends at the southeastern edge. U.S. 60 and U.S. 119 run through the center. Yeager Airport is about two miles north of the interstates on route 114, Amtrak's Cardinal stops in the city, and the Kanawha Valley Regional Transportation Authority runs the buses.

Kanawha County Schools runs the public schools. Call the district to confirm the school assignment for a specific address.

faqs.q: Does the City of Charleston or Kanawha County collect property tax?
faqs.a: Kanawha County does. The Sheriff's Tax Division at 409 Virginia Street East takes payments, and its phone number is 304-357-0210.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit for a roof or window replacement in Charleston?
faqs.a: Yes. Roofs and replacement windows are on the Building Department's permit list, and fees are waived only when the total job cost is $2,500 or less.

faqs.q: How can I tell whether a Charleston house is in a flood zone?
faqs.a: Ask the city's Floodplain Manager for a determination, or use the state's flood hazard tool. A property in a Special Flood Hazard Area typically needs flood insurance, and an Elevation Certificate can help with premiums.

faqs.q: What transfer tax applies when I sell a Charleston house?
faqs.a: The base rates are $1.10 per $500 of value plus 55 cents per $500 for the county, plus a $20 fee, unless the Kanawha County Commission has raised its rate. The seller pays unless the buyer takes the deed with the tax unpaid.

faqs.q: When do Kanawha County property tax payments come due?
faqs.a: September 1 and March 1, with a 2.5 percent discount for paying before each date. Unpaid halves turn delinquent on October 1 and April 1 and accrue 9 percent interest.
